details:
What it does. HuellaX is a candidate-first web lab for NASA’s SPHEREx data. In Sky View, you pick a region of the sky and an epoch on a 3D globe and a UTC timeline. You then send that selection to MoveScope with one link. MoveScope compares several epochs to find sources that move, then scores each one with its speed, uncertainty and significance. Every candidate is checked against Gaia DR3 (0.5″ crossmatch), 2MASS/WISE and SkyBoT/IMCCE for known Solar System objects. It gets one clear status: known, ambiguous, no match, insufficient, unavailable or conflict. The SPHEREx 102-band coverage from 0.75 to 5 µm and the molecular windows sit right inside Sky View. Batch mode builds a unified candidate catalogue that you can export to CSV or JSON.

Benefits. Preparing SPHEREx data by hand takes about 30 minutes per object, or 15 hours for 30 objects. HuellaX brings that down to minutes, with no coding needed. Students, citizen scientists and researchers can all go from raw sky to a checked candidate.

Intended impact. HuellaX opens SPHEREx’s all-sky, repeated infrared survey to more people, helps find moving objects (Planet X-type searches), and teaches good scientific practice.

Creativity. The tool follows one rule: candidate ≠ discovery. It shows its own limits (6.15″/pixel, catalogue coverage), lists what would disprove each result, and never turns a non-match into a claim. It works in English and Spanish.

Tools. Web app with SQL-backed catalogues, Aladin sky maps, IRSA/SPHEREx, Gaia, 2MASS/WISE and SkyBoT APIs, and a 3D globe. Open source on GitHub: https://github.com/Beltranpcb/HuellaX

Factors considered. Scientific honesty, data provenance and labels for real versus synthetic data, accessibility, two languages, and handling external services when they don’t respond
